data.additional_information:
We are seeking a Mobility & Vehicle Dynamics Engineer to lead the design and analysis of locomotion systems for our Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs), Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs), and Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUVs). The role spans powertrain integration, suspension, steering, terrain-interaction modelling, hydrodynamics for marine platforms, and end-to-end vehicle dynamics. 
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

1. Vehicle Architecture & Mobility Design: Define mobility architecture for UGVs (wheeled / tracked / legged) and marine platforms — drive layout, suspension geometry, steering kinematics, and powertrain topology. 
2. Vehicle Dynamics Modelling: Build multi-body dynamics models. Simulate ride, handling, traction, slip, and stability across operating conditions. 
3. Marine Platform Hydrodynamics (if applicable): For USV/UUV programs: hull resistance, seakeeping, manoeuvring, and propulsion (thrusters, water-jets, ducted props). Run CFD-based hydrodynamic studies and correlate with test data. 
4. Powertrain Integration: Size and integrate electric / hybrid powertrains: motor, gearbox, ESC/inverter, battery, and thermal management — across mission profiles and duty cycles. 
5. Terrain & Environment Interaction: Develop terramechanics models for off-road UGVs, water-soil interaction for amphibious systems, and environmental load cases for vehicle qualification. 
6. Testing & Field Validation: Plan and execute field tests for traction, stability, manoeuvrability, and endurance. Reduce test data and feed it back into improved vehicle models. 
7. Documentation & Certification Support: Prepare design notes, technical reports, and certification documents in line with applicable airworthiness standards (DGCA, MIL-HDBK, MILSTD, STANAG references). 
8. Collaboration and Communication: Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams for design intent, specifications, and technical concepts of the product. 9
IP Development & Knowledge Building: Contribute to Patents and Internal design guidelines 

Skills Required 

1. Strong fundamentals in vehicle dynamics, powertrain engineering, and multi-body dynamics. 
2. Familiarity with electric vehicle architectures: motors, inverters, batteries, BMS, and thermal management. 
3. (For marine focus) Working knowledge of ship hydrodynamics, seakeeping, and resistance methods; CFD experience. 
4. Understanding of terramechanics or soil-vehicle interaction for off-road UGV design.
5. Familiarity with control systems and how mobility hardware interfaces with autonomy stacks (drive-by-wire, traction control). 
6. Ability to communicate technical decisions clearly across mechanical, autonomy, and electronics teams. 
7. Ability to lead, collaborate, and communicate effectively across disciplines. 
8.Team Player: Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, cross-functional team environment. Willingness to learn from and contribute to the knowledge of others

Educational Qualification- PhD/M.tech/M.E
Required Experience- 0-2 Yrs
data.additional_details:
Please find below the additional important details regarding our Company Clauses & Policies:

1.NDA – Non-Disclosure Agreement
Candidates must not disclose or share any confidential information related to their job role, projects, company operations, or work responsibilities with any external party. This clause will remain applicable for a lifetime.
2.NCC – Non-Compete Clause
Upon joining the company, when you decide to leave the organization in the future, you will not be eligible to join any direct competitor of the company for a period of 3 years post the last working day.
3.Minimum Service Agreement – 2 Years
Candidates from any branch having less than 2 Years of Experience are required to sign a mandatory 2-year Minimum Service Agreement. However, Candidates with more than 2 years of prior experience are exempted from the Minimum Service Agreement. Additionally breach of this agreement will result in a financial penalty of 40% of the CTC.
